headline: Silicon bid and software sold split tech while September stays a coin-flip hike

sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## Silicon is bid, software is sold — the week's story is inside tech
The one development worth naming is dispersion within technology, not a macro shock. Weekly sector reads dated 2026-09-04 show hardware leading and software lagging in the same tape. Memory/Storage is +7.6 (+7.5% vs SPY), all four members — STX, WDC, MU, SNDK — participating; Foundry +5.4 (+5.3%, INTC, TSEM, TSM, UMC, 4 of 4); Computer/GPU +3.4 (+3.3%, 6 of 6). Against that, Cybersecurity is −6.9 (−7.0%, NET, S, CRWD, PANW) and Software/SaaS −4.7 (−4.8%, ADBE, FIG, NOW, SHOP, ZM, CRM). XLK printed +0.9 on the week (+0.7 excess) while SPY did +0.1, so the tech-index gain is silicon-driven, not broad.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body: The within-tech read holds while Memory/Storage stays above +0 vs SPY and Software/SaaS stays below it; a convergence either way breaks it. ADBE and ORCL post-close 2026-09-10 are the near test — both sit on the software side, so their prints check whether the weakness is a repricing or a dip. On the macro side, front-end odds drifting below 50% hike into 9/16 would ease the pressure on rate-sensitive software; odds pushing toward the 12/9 hike path would deepen it. No live spot, rate or tide printed this run, so these are frozen levels, not intraday confirmation.
